name: wings-d6116827-blind29
instr:
# pterodactyl/wings: tracking down widespread daemon misbehaviour without a test suite

A node built from this tree runs game instances on a host, looks after the data those instances keep, talks to the control panel above it, and carries their console output out to whoever is watching. Ordinary day-to-day use now produces a broad spread of wrong answers across all of that. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits.

Opening a stored document for writing while a size cap is in force, then writing through the handle that comes back, mis-accounts nearly everything. A write that would carry the document past the cap is refused, yet it claims one byte written rather than none, and the running usage figure left behind afterwards does not match the bytes actually stored. A write aimed far beyond the end of a document, which fails as expected, drags the recorded usage down to a tiny number instead of leaving the earlier figure alone, and closing a handle after shortening a document leaves the figure wrong as well. Writing a whole document from an incoming feed in one go goes the same way: the bytes land on disk intact, yet the storage accounted to that instance afterwards differs from the number of bytes written. Reading a stored document back through the node is broken separately: opening one to read it, or to stat it, hands back a reader already positioned a byte past the start, so the content that comes out is missing its first byte.
